thread.title: Chip Stocks Have Jitters As Earnings Season Kicks Off

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Chip Stocks Have Jitters As Earnings Season Kicks Off

organizations.name: chip stocks have jitters as earnings season kicks off chip

text:
Chip stocks are hoping for some much-needed good news in the week ahead as earnings season shifts into high gear.
X The week ahead will bring earnings reports from a bunch of closely watched chip companies, including Texas Instruments ( TXN ) on Tuesday, Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) and Qualcomm ( QCOM ) on Wednesday, and Intel ( INTC ) on Thursday.
The sector was knocked down over the past week by cautious reports from chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( TSM ) and semiconductor-equipment supplier Lam Research ( LRCX ).
Investors fret the chip sector has peaked and is starting to enter a down cycle, analysts say.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Taiwan Semi, the world's largest contract chipmaker, added to those concerns on Thursday when it lowered its target for sales growth in the global semiconductor industry this year to 5%, down from its prior outlook for 5% to 7% growth.
Big Drop For Chip Index That day, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 4.3%. It was the biggest one-day drop for the index, known as SOX, since Feb. 8 and only the 10th time in the past eight years when the index fell more than 4%.
The iShares PHLX Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) fell 1.2% on the stock market today .
The broad sell-off in the chip sector was not justified, Needham analyst Rajvindra Gill said in a report Friday. Taiwan Semi said the sales weakness was related mostly to the smartphone sector, particularly Apple ( AAPL ). The chipmaker said sector growth areas like automotive, Internet of Things and data centers remained strong, Gill said.
Lam Research also rattled chip stocks when it gave a disappointing outlook late Tuesday for chip-gear shipments for the rest of the year. Fremont, Calif.-based Lam makes wafer fabrication equipment for the semiconductor industry.
Chip Stocks Heading Lower? Bank of America Merrill Lynch on Friday said chip stocks could go 4% to 7% lower. Rough earnings, trade fights and market volatility have "soured the mood," analyst Vivek Arya said in a report.
Arya cut his price targets on chip stocks with heavy exposure to Apple's iPhone business, including Broadcom ( AVGO ), Cirrus Logic ( CRUS ) and Skyworks Solutions ( SWKS ).
Chip company earnings in the week ahead could decide if the sector rebounds or continues its downward trajectory.
Dallas-based Texas Instruments is set to report first-quarter results after the market close Tuesday. Analysts expect TI to earn $1.11 a share, up 14% year over year. That's on sales of $3.65 billion, up 7%, in the March quarter.
AMD Heading Into The Black? Analysts say Santa Clara, Calif.-based AMD should earn 9 cents a share, reversing a year-earlier loss of 4 cents a share. That's on sales of $1.57 billion, up 59%, in its fiscal first quarter.
Wall Street expects San Diego-based Qualcomm to earn 70 cents a share, down 48%, on sales of $5.19 billion, down 13%, in its fiscal second quarter.
A legal dispute with major customer Apple has dampened its results in recent quarters. Apple refuses to pay technology licensing fees to Qualcomm until the legal matter is resolved.
Also weighing on Qualcomm is the possibility that China could block its proposed acquisition of NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ). On Thursday, China's Ministry of Commerce gave a pessimistic preliminary review of the Qualcomm-NXP deal.
Analysts see Santa Clara, Calif.-based Intel earning 72 cents a share, up 9%, on sales of $15.05 billion, up 2%, in the first quarter.
